assertions.text: Discount ladder, and traveller eligibility are in separate tables. Rolling window counting as a third table is desirable.
assertions.evidence: Separate @TableTest methods: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount

assertions.text: Children's flat 20% discount is represented.
assertions.evidence: "Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips   | CHILD              | {1, 5, 40}       | 20"

assertions.text: Multiple tiers derived from 'every fifth trip' rule, with boundaries/value sets; max 40% represented.
assertions.evidence: "Exactly at the cap | 40 | 40" and "Beyond the cap stays capped | {41, 45, 100} | 40"

assertions.text: 30-day rolling window boundary tested: 30 days included, 31 days excluded.
assertions.evidence: "Exactly 30 days ago is still in window ... | 1" and "31 days ago has fallen out of the window ... | 0"

assertions.text: 30-day window exercised at time-of-purchase granularity (sub-day distinction), not just whole days.
assertions.evidence: Only whole-day rows exist: "30/SINGLE/ZONE_1" vs "31/SINGLE/ZONE_1"; no hour-level distinction like 29d23h vs 30d1h

assertions.text: Value sets in tier table contain exactly the values producing the same discount, no cross-tier contamination.
Discount ladder table uses value sets for ticket count column to group counts within a tier.
assertions.evidence: "Below first tier | {1, 2, 3, 4} | 0" and similar grouped value sets throughout discountForTripCount table

assertions.text: Tier-to-discount mapping expressed once, not repeated across multiple tables.
assertions.evidence: Full ladder enumerated only in discountForTripCount; other tables use only a few sample points for dispatch/integration checks

assertions.text: @DisplayName is present on test methods, OR method names read as clear descriptive titles when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 4 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: @Description present with context beyond restating columns.
assertions.evidence: "The trip ladder: every 5th single ticket in the rolling 30-day window (counting the ticket being purchased now) raises the discount by 5%, up to a 40% cap."

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Eligibility/passenger-type table includes a Zone column (value set) showing discount applies regardless of zone.
assertions.evidence: discountForCategoryAndTripCount table columns are only "Traveler Category | Trips In Window | Discount?" — no Zone column

assertions.text: The rolling-window counting concern shows by row that a past purchase's zone does not affect whether it counts toward the travel count
assertions.evidence: "Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3"

assertions.text: Adult and senior are expressed as a value set {ADULT, SENIOR}
assertions.evidence: "Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40"

assertions.text: All 9 discount tiers are represented in the ladder table
assertions.evidence: Table jumps from 'Exactly at second tier | 10 | 10' directly to 'Exactly at seventh tier | 35 | 35', omitting tiers 15/20/25/30

assertions.text: Each tier in the discount ladder is expressed as a single row with a value set
assertions.evidence: "Exactly at first tier | 5 | 5" and "Within first tier | {6, 7, 8, 9} | 5" split the same tier across two rows

assertions.text: The rolling window table expresses time relatively
assertions.evidence: "[1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 15/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 29/SINGLE/ZONE_1]" encodes days-ago per entry, parsed via converter as days before purchase

assertions.text: Multiple tables each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: Four @TableTest methods: discountForTripCount, countSingleTicketsInWindow, discountForCategoryAndTripCount, calculatesDiscountEndToEnd

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules
assertions.evidence: countSingleTicketsInWindow table has 7 focused rows testing only window/ticket-type/zone rules, no category mixing

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable
assertions.evidence: "Below first tier | {1, 2, 3, 4} | 0" - expectation 0 is not a copy of input value set, and values vary across rows (0,5,10,35,40)

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body
assertions.evidence: @Description states "every 5th single ticket... raises the discount by 5%... up to a 40% cap" and "trailing 30 days"

assertions.text: Each @DisplayName states what the code under test does
assertions.evidence: Method names like "discountForTripCount", "countSingleTicketsInWindow", "calculatesDiscountEndToEnd" describe computed behavior

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: A value the rule's outcome depends on, and which the table holds constant for every row, must be visible as a column or named in the @DisplayName/@Description as deliberately held fixed.
assertions.evidence: PURCHASE_TIME is fixed as a field, but all history entries are expressed as days-ago (e.g. `1/SINGLE/ZONE_1`) relative to it, so the outcome is indifferent to its literal value; TypeConverter also hardcodes TravelerCategory.ADULT for history entries, but countSingleTicketsInWindow(history, purchaseTime) takes no traveler category, so this cannot affect the outcome either.

assertions.text: When a title or description quantifies over a domain, the rows must actually cover that domain.
assertions.evidence: "Zone must never affect the count." is backed by row "Zone does not affect the count | [1/SINGLE/ZONE_1, 2/SINGLE/ZONE_2, 3/SINGLE/ZONE_3] | 3"; "CHILD always gets a flat 20% discount, independent of travel frequency" is backed by "Child gets a flat discount regardless of trips | CHILD | {1, 5, 40} | 20"; "ADULT and SENIOR are treated identically" is backed by "Adult and senior are capped the same | {ADULT, SENIOR} | 45 | 40".
